competencies.text: Develop family and community-based DRRM plans.

days.title: DRRM Planning Basics
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to explain what Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (DRRM) is, identify its four thematic pillars, and describe how families and communities can prepare for disasters.

🛡️ What Is DRRM?

Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (DRRM) is the systematic approach to reducing the damage caused by natural and human-made hazards. It focuses on prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery.

The Philippines has RA 10121 — the Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010 — which institutionalized DRRM nationwide.

🏛️ The Four Thematic Pillars of DRRM

PillarFocusExamples
1. Prevention & MitigationReduce or avoid the impact of hazardsBuilding codes, hazard maps, reforestation, drainage systems
2. PreparednessPrepare people and systems to respond effectivelyDrills, early warning systems, Go Bags, evacuation plans
3. ResponseImmediate actions during and after a disasterSearch and rescue, relief distribution, medical aid, evacuation
4. Rehabilitation & RecoveryRestore normal life after a disasterRebuilding homes, restoring livelihoods, psychological support

👨‍👩‍👧 Family-Based DRRM Plan

Every family should have an emergency plan. Key components:

  1. Designate a meeting point — inside and outside your community.
  2. Assign roles — who brings the Go Bag? Who checks on lolo/lola? Who turns off utilities?
  3. List emergency contacts — barangay, LGU, NDRRMC, PAGASA, PHIVOLCS hotlines.
  4. Prepare a Go Bag — ready to grab at any time.
  5. Know your evacuation route — and practice it twice a year.
  6. Backup important documents — IDs, birth certificates, land titles — keep copies in a waterproof bag or cloud storage.
  7. Plan for vulnerable members — elderly, PWDs, infants, pregnant women, and pets.

🎒 The Go Bag Checklist

CategoryItems
Water & Food1 gallon water per person (3 days), non-perishable food (canned goods, biscuits, energy bars), manual can opener
CommunicationBattery-powered radio, extra batteries, fully charged power bank, whistle
LightFlashlight, headlamp, extra batteries
First AidBandages, antiseptic, prescription medicines, pain relievers, thermometer
DocumentsCopies of IDs, birth certificates, insurance, list of emergency contacts (in waterproof bag)
ClothingLight clothing, rain jacket, sturdy shoes, blanket, towel
OthersCash, multi-tool, face masks, hygiene kit, duct tape

🏘️ Community-Based DRRM Plan

Barangays and LGUs also need DRRM plans, including:

  • Hazard mapping — know which areas flood, slide, or are exposed to surges.
  • Early warning systems — sirens, SMS alerts, community flags.
  • Evacuation centers — schools, barangay halls, churches — with capacity for vulnerable groups.
  • Trained responders — Barangay Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Committee (BDRRMC).
  • Stockpiles — food, water, medicines, blankets, generators.
  • Drills — quarterly earthquake, fire, and typhoon drills.

⚠️ Climate Change Adaptation in DRRM

As climate change makes hazards more intense and unpredictable, DRRM must also adapt:

  • Nature-based solutions: Mangrove restoration, urban forests, watershed protection.
  • Resilient infrastructure: Elevated roads, flood-proof buildings, drainage upgrades.
  • Climate-resilient agriculture: Salt-tolerant rice, drought-resistant corn.
  • Insurance and safety nets: Crop insurance, emergency cash transfers.

🇵🇭 Key Agencies in Philippine DRRM

  • NDRRMC — coordinates national disaster response.
  • PAGASA — weather and climate warnings.
  • PHIVOLCS — earthquake, volcano, tsunami warnings.
  • DSWD — relief distribution and social protection.
  • DOH — health emergency response.
  • DepEd — school safety and class suspensions.
  • DILG — supports LGUs and barangays in DRRM.

📌 Quick Check

  • What are the four thematic pillars of DRRM? (Answer: Prevention & Mitigation, Preparedness, Response, Rehabilitation & Recovery)
  • What is a Go Bag? (Answer: an emergency kit with essentials ready to grab in case of evacuation)
  • Which Philippine law institutionalized DRRM? (Answer: RA 10121 — DRRM Act of 2010)

days.title: Match Game — DRRM Components
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each DRRM concept, pillar, or agency to its correct description. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Systematic approach to reducing disaster damage — prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, recovery
Pillar focused on reducing or avoiding hazard impacts — like building codes and reforestation
Pillar focused on drills, early warning systems, Go Bags, and evacuation plans
Pillar focused on immediate actions during and after a disaster — search and rescue
Pillar focused on restoring normal life — rebuilding homes, restoring livelihoods
Emergency kit with water, food, radio, flashlight, medicines, and documents
Barangay Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Committee — first responders at the community level

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Family Emergency Plan
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🌀 A Signal No. 3 typhoon is approaching your province in 24 hours. What should your family do FIRST?

choices.label: A) Review the family DRRM plan, prepare the Go Bag, secure the house, and monitor PAGASA updates
B) Wait until the typhoon is directly overhead
C) Go to the mall to buy supplies during peak hours
D) Ignore the warning — typhoons pass quickly

scenario.text: 🎒 Your family is preparing a Go Bag. Which item should NEVER be left out?

choices.label: A) Drinking water and non-perishable food for at least 3 days
B) Video game console
C) Formal party dress
D) Extra shoes

scenario.text: 🏫 Your barangay has an earthquake drill scheduled. Why is it important to participate?

choices.label: A) Drills build muscle memory — during a real earthquake, you'll know to Drop, Cover, and Hold
B) Drills are just for fun
C) They replace the need for a Go Bag
D) They aren't important

scenario.text: 👵 Your grandmother uses a wheelchair. How should she be included in the family DRRM plan?

choices.label: A) Assign someone to help her evacuate, ensure accessible routes, and prepare her medicines in the Go Bag
B) Leave her at home during evacuation
C) Ignore her needs
D) Hope for the best

scenario.text: 🌳 A coastal barangay plants mangroves along the shoreline. What DRRM pillar does this activity fall under?

choices.label: A) Prevention & Mitigation — mangroves reduce storm surge and coastal erosion
B) Response — they help during rescue
C) Recovery — they rebuild homes
D) It doesn't fit any pillar

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the DRRM Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the DRRM Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. This is your final formative check before the Term Exam.

choices.label: A) Disaster Risk Reduction and Management
B) Department of Regional Risk Measures
C) Disaster Response and Recovery Method
D) Direct Rescue and Relief Management

escape.text: How many thematic pillars make up the DRRM framework?

choices.label: A) Four
B) Two
C) Six
D) Ten

escape.text: Which pillar focuses on drills, Go Bags, and evacuation plans?

choices.label: A) Preparedness
B) Response
C) Recovery
D) Prevention
A) RA 10121 — Philippine DRRM Act of 2010

escape.text: What should a family do FIRST when a typhoon warning is issued?

choices.label: A) Review the DRRM plan, prepare the Go Bag, secure the house, and monitor PAGASA
B) Wait until the last minute
C) Go outside and watch the storm
D) Ignore warnings

escape.text: Which activity is an example of MITIGATION in DRRM?

choices.label: A) Planting mangroves to reduce storm surge impact
B) Distributing relief goods after a typhoon
C) Rebuilding houses after a flood
D) Conducting search and rescue
